literal: Fittingly having investigated, in a manner that [the crime] does not proceed again, proportionately punishing is [the duty of] the king.
translation: A true ruler is one who thoroughly investigates an offense and administers a proportionate punishment, ensuring that the crime is not repeated.
modern: ஒரு குற்றத்தை நடுநிலையோடு ஆராய்ந்து, மீண்டும் அக்குற்றம் நடக்காதவாறு, அதற்குப் பொருத்தமான தண்டனையை வழங்குவதே சிறந்த அரசனின் கடமையாகும்.
explanation: This couplet outlines the core principles of justice and deterrence for a ruler. The word 'தக்காங்கு' emphasizes that the investigation must be conducted fittingly and impartially. The phrase 'தலைச்செல்லா வண்ணத்தால்' highlights the goal of deterrence, meaning the punishment should be designed so that the crime does not occur again. Finally, 'ஒத்தாங்கு ஒறுப்பது' demands that the punishment be perfectly proportionate to the gravity of the offense, ensuring justice is neither overly harsh nor weak.
